items.body:
Custom-built for sunny days, Sofie Birch’s solo Stroom debut melds bossa and psych pops with delicate touches of 4th world ambient jazz and chamber music in a chiffon-layered, naïf dream sequence landing somewhere on the line between Sam Prekop's self-titled alltimer, Antena's Camino Del Sol x Stereolab on the downbeat...

"This album is created over the past years with my brother Alfred. This period has been spiritually transformative for me. it reflects the playfulness and authenticity that comes out of releasing deep traumas and healing wounds. this music comes from a deep place of joy and connection with my brother and with the essense of being a child. being filter free and in contact with the most uncomplicated and loving parts of ourselves, still emphasizing magic and mystery, like childhood does without asking for permission or confirmation.

It took me a while to actually see the music as an interconnected piece. i have been taking in and out material, re mixing, removing, rearranging, re producing and regretting all along the way. but suddenly when we mastered this selection on a cassette tape recorder, the meaning started to reveal itself and drawing threads back in time.

Bivabippalukka is playfulness, intuition, transition and myths. the page of cups. the ideas rising, the energy flowing, flowers, stars and jumping creatures on the verge of dimensions. fortune telling, magic cards, secret caves and things that disappear right in front of you. many talented guests playing with me and my visions on the album.

Bossa nova is the most comforting genre for me. and we need comfort in these times. we need comfort to heal and feel joy to be able to keep dreaming and manifesting - and transmuting the world.

I am not gonna play this music live in the form it appears. i will still continue playing spiritual ambient music. this work is something else. it is pocket of joy, a cup with a fish. it is a step on the journey, like everything else."
items._genre: ambient / bossa nova / fourth world / chamber pop
items._cn_summary: 这是Sofie Birch在独立厂牌Stroom的首张个人专辑，将bossa nova与迷幻流行融合，并加入第四世界氛围爵士与室内音乐元素，营造出轻盈如薄纱的梦境质感。艺术家本人阐述该作是与兄长Alfred多年合作的结晶，以孩童般的直觉与游戏精神为核心，主题围绕释放创伤、疗愈与喜悦展开，涵盖塔罗意象、自然元素与神秘叙事。制作过程中经过反复取舍重混，最终通过卡带母带处理揭示了作品的内在连贯性。专辑邀请多位乐手参与，呈现融合直觉创作与神秘学想象的声音世界。整体定位偏向温柔舒适的跨界融合，虽具个人美学但与极端实验路线距离较远。

Bassbin veteran Om Unit flexes his authority on a tracky, jacking rework of ‘Trust’ built to sound loud and in charge on a big rig, kinda reminding of Fis-T’s UKF joints, wobbles included, whereas Eris Drew gives a proggy, breaksy house redraw of ‘Wiggler’ like a ruggeder Josh Wink cut built for haughty circuit canter.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了两首对Hodge原曲的重混音作品。Om Unit的混音偏向低频厚重、节奏驱动的club techno路线，强调大音量系统下的冲击力，音色处理让人联想到早期Fis-T的UK bass美学，低频wobble元素贯穿始终。Eris Drew的混音则更为渐进式，将house结构与碎拍元素融合，节奏编排复杂，带有Josh Wink式的高傲律动感，整体更适合大型舞池的持续推进。两位制作人各自展现了不同的技术取向，但两首混音的共同点在于都保留了原作的骨骼结构，在此基础上进行了风格化的扩展。对于偏好实验性电子乐的人来说，混音版本提供了一些有趣的音色探索，但整体仍属于功能性舞曲范畴，创新程度有限。

items.body:
Amsterdam electronic music institution Dekmantel is heading to Southeast Asia for the first time, teaming up with Desa Potato Head Bali for a one-day takeover in Seminyak.

Set for 26 September, the collaboration will bring a full day of electronic music and cultural programming to Potato Head Beach Club and Klymax, culminating in a night party headlined by Avalon Emerson, who will also make her Southeast Asian debut.

The takeover comes after years of exchanges between the Dekmantel and Potato Head teams. Dekmantel founder Casper van Tielrooij and Interstellar Funk's Olf van Elden have previously spent time in Bali, while the Potato Head team has visited Amsterdam for Dekmantel Festival.

Joining Avalon Emerson on the bill are Dekmantel Soundsystem, Fafi Abdel Nour, Ogazón, Soichi Terada, Danny Satria, Archie, Bagvs, Dita, Kaazi, Kiwed, and Sattle, bringing together artists from Europe, the US, Japan, and Indonesia.

The programme will stretch beyond the dancefloor, with daytime listening sessions, live Q&As, and a Desa Dialogue centred on ideas, culture, and creativity. The festivities will then move into the night across Potato Head Beach Club and Klymax.

The event will also spotlight artists from Bali and Indonesia, including Danny Satria, Dita, Kiwed, and Sattle. Archie and Bagvs will team up for a B2B set spanning deep house, minimal techno, spaced-out disco, and beyond, while Danny Satria will perform live.

Japan's Soichi Terada will also present his live set, while Dekmantel Soundsystem will reunite van Tielrooij and Olf van Elden behind the decks.

"It started as a friendship. We've spent years visiting each other, sharing music, sharing spaces, and now we get to share Bali with them," shared Potato Head resident DJ Dita. "It feels like the most natural thing! And also very much overdue."

The event will conclude with Avalon Emerson, whose sets move across house, techno, new wave, disco, and deep rave, closing out Dekmantel's first outing in Southeast Asia.

Tickets can be purchased here.

items.body: Can has shared “Arles 75 Sechs”, a track from the forthcoming live album “Live in Arles 1975”, out 25 September 2026 via Mute and the band’s own Spoon Records on double vinyl, CD and digital. The album documents a 1975 concert at the Théâtre Antique d’Arles in the South of France, and “Arles 75 Sechs” is the sixth of six tracks on the record. Founding keyboardist Irmin Schmidt recalled the performance: “I remember a very beautiful atmosphere. It was a summer night in the South of France, everybody was stoned and the atmosphere was very special.” “Live in Arles 1975” originates from a fan recording of the show and features the core lineup of Irmin Schmidt, Jaki Liebezeit, Michael Karoli and Holger Czukay. The concert was supported by Nico & Kevin Ayers and Ash Ra Tempel, and is remembered in the sleeve notes by two attendees, including author and journalist Pascal Bussy. The tracklist runs “Arles 75 Eins”, “Arles 75 Zwei”, “Arles 75 Drei”, “Arles 75 Vier”, “Arles 75 Fünf” and “Arles 75 Sechs”. Full release details, including format and pre-order information, were covered in Side-Line’s earlier report: Can announce “Live in Arles 1975”, out 25 September via Mute. Can Live series continues “Live in Arles 1975” is the latest in a series of archival live albums assembled by Schmidt and producer/engineer René Tinner from the Spoon Records vaults and fan recordings. Previous volumes in the series include “Can Live in Stuttgart 1975”, “Can Live in Cuxhaven 1976”, “Can Live in Brighton 1975”, “Can Live in Paris 1973” (the first to feature the late Damo Suzuki), “Can Live in Aston 1977” and “Can Live in Keele 1977” (2024). About Can Can formed in Cologne, West Germany, in 1968, founded by Irmin Schmidt (keyboards) and Holger Czukay (bass), both former students of composer Karlheinz Stockhausen, together with Michael Karoli (guitar) and Jaki Liebezeit (drums). The band’s early vocalists were Malcolm Mooney and, from 1970, Damo Suzuki. Can released a run of studio albums through the 1970s, including “Monster Movie” (1969), “Tago Mago” (1971), “Ege Bamyasi” (1972) and “Future Days” (1973), before disbanding in the early 1980s. Since 2020, Mute and Spoon Records have issued a series of archival live recordings drawn from the band’s touring years, beginning with “Can Live in Stuttgart 1975” and continuing through “Can Live in Cuxhaven 1976”, “Can Live in Brighton 1975”, “Can Live in Paris 1973”, “Can Live in Aston 1977” and “Can Live in Keele 1977”. Irmin Schmidt, the band’s last surviving founding member, has also continued to release solo work, including the 2026 album “Requiem” on Mute, covered previously by Side-Line. “Live in Arles 1975”, out 25 September 2026, extends the live series with a recording from the band’s 1975 concert in the South of France.
items._cn_summary: 本文是关于Can乐队1975年法国阿尔勒古剧场演出现场录音专辑发行的新闻稿。专辑《Live in Arles 1975》收录六首以德语数字编号命名的曲目，由核心成员Irmin Schmidt、Jaki Liebezeit、Michael Karoli和Holger Czukay演奏。录音源自粉丝录制，由Schmidt与制作人René Tinner从Spoon Records档案中整理。Irmin Schmidt回忆演出当晚氛围迷幻而独特。该专辑是Mute与Spoon Records自2020年以来持续发行的Can现场档案系列之一，此前已发行多张1970年代不同时期的现场录音。文章同时提供了Can乐队的简短背景介绍，提及乐队与作曲家Stockhausen的渊源以及经典专辑。整篇内容以资讯发布为主，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评析。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张芬兰手风琴与钢琴二重奏专辑，两人合作长达三十五年，默契已臻化境。专辑以传统曲调和原创作品交替展开，Kalaniemi的旋律感细腻而敏锐，Alakotila的钢琴伴奏则在支撑之余加入自己的呼吸，使每首作品被打磨成光泽流丽的珠玉。手风琴与钢琴的对话在大部分时间里保持极简的编制，仅在标题曲中引入弦乐四重奏作适度扩展。整体氛围宁静、绵长、略带梦幻感，既不追求炫技，也不强调戏剧张力，音乐服务于旋律本身。Piazzolla的《Oblivion》为专辑带来一丝阴影，Alakotila的《Tango Berlin》则呼应了芬兰人对探戈的偏爱。整张专辑不试图震撼听者，而是营造一种安稳而持续的流动感。

items.body: Karlsruhe, Germany industrial death-wave trio Bleak Monday has released a video for Shelter, a single issued on Bandcamp on July 31, 2026. The track is drawn from Bleak Monday’s upcoming debut album, “Bad Music”, which does not yet have a confirmed release date. The video for “Shelter” was directed by Natascha Gaballo. It is the latest visual release from the band, which has built its catalogue independently since forming in December 2022. “Shelter” follows Bleak Monday’s 2024 single “Human Needs”, released December 13, 2024, and the band’s earlier EP “flies”. The new track continues the project’s industrial death-wave sound, pairing distorted guitar and synth textures with vocalist Kim Ryder’s delivery. About Bleak Monday Bleak Monday formed in Karlsruhe, Germany, in December 2022. The trio is made up of Kim Ryder (vocals), Yann Lauer (guitar and feedback) and Sebastian “Hubu” Huber (synths, drums and bass). The band began playing live in early 2023 and has since shared stages with acts including Das Kinn, Nils Keppel, The Body and Ministry. Bleak Monday released its debut EP, “flies”, followed by the single “Human Needs” on December 13, 2024. Both releases, along with “Shelter”, are self-released through the band’s Bandcamp page. “Shelter” is presented as an early single from Bleak Monday’s forthcoming debut album, “Bad Music”.

items.body: Project Pitchfork, the Hamburg group that mixes dark wave, electro-industrial and dark electro elements, released “Quantum Mechanics” on 12 August 2011 through Trisol. The album turns 15 this year. It arrived one year after “Continuum Ride” (2010) and appeared on CD, as a strictly limited double-CD book edition of 2,000 copies, and digitally. Peter Spilles wrote and produced the album, Chris von Rautenkranz mastered it at Soundgarden Tonstudio, Ingo Römling created the artwork and Jens Howorka took the band photography. The ten-track album runs “Freeze in Silence,” “Lament,” “Run for Cover,” “Radical Business,” “Mute Spectators,” “Quantum Mechanics,” “The Queen of Time and Space,” “Splice,” “We Will Descend” and “You Rest in My Heart.” The book edition, bound with thread stitching and packed with a 40-page booklet of lyrics and additional artwork, adds a bonus disc holding the exclusive tracks “Tempest” and “Insomnia,” remixes of “Freeze in Silence,” “Run for Cover” and “Lament,” and an instrumental version of the title track. In December 2019, Trisol reissued “Quantum Mechanics” as a limited 2LP and 2CD set. The album streams on Spotify. About Project Pitchfork Project Pitchfork started in Hamburg, Germany, where vocalist and composer Peter Spilles and keyboardist Dirk Scheuber began collaborating in 1989. The pair played their first concert in Hamburg in February 1990 and recorded the demo “K.N.K.A.” that same year. Their debut album “Dhyani” followed in May 1991 on Hypnobeat, and 1992 brought both “Lam-‘Bras,” which introduced vocalist Patricia Nigiani, and “Entities.” In 1994 the band moved to Off Beat for “IO,” whose singles “Renascence” and “Carrion” brought them into the German charts. A year later they founded their own imprint Candyland Entertainment, issued “Alpha Omega” and supported Rammstein on selected tour dates. The late 1990s produced “¡Chakra:Red!” and the concept album “Eon:Eon,” while the 2000s added “Daimonion,” the “NUN” trilogy built around “Inferno,” and “Kaskade” (2005). On Trisol, the group released “Dream, Tiresias!” and “Continuum Ride” before “Quantum Mechanics” arrived in August 2011. “Black” (2013), “Blood” (2014) and “Look Up, I’m Down There” (2016) followed, and the space-oriented trilogy of “Akkretion,” “Fragment” and “Elysium” was completed in 2024. The current line-up centres on Peter Spilles with keyboardist Jürgen Jansen and drummers Achim Färber and Christian “Leo” Leonhardt; co-founder Dirk Scheuber left the group in 2021. The 15th anniversary of “Quantum Mechanics” places the album back in that timeline, early in the band’s 2010s run on Trisol.

items.body:
Japan’s classic knack for slick jazz emulation is in debonaire effect on The Milky Way’s 1979 suite of bossanova and elegant city pop, produced by guitarist Makoto Matsushita and ambient pioneer Yasuaki Shimizu. Last available on LP 10 years ago, now trading for triple figures 2nd hand…

“Wewantsounds is delighted to present the first official reissue of the highly sought-after 1979 classic, Summer-Time Love Song by The Milky Way. Originally released on the Seven Seas label in Japan and produced by the legendary Makoto Matsushita—the visionary behind the cult masterpiece First Light —the album is a premier example of the sophisticated sound that defined the era. Featuring the cream of Japanese musicians, including Yasuaki Shimizu, the record offers a superb mix of AOR, jazz fusion, funk, and bossa nova. Remastered for vinyl by Colorsound Studio, this deluxe reissue features the original artwork, an 8 page booklet with a new introduction by Paul Bowler.”
items._genre: city pop / bossa nova / jazz fusion / AOR
items._cn_summary: 这张1979年日本专辑由吉他手松本慎制作，环境音乐先驱的清水靖晃参与演奏，以精致的bossa nova和city pop风格展现那个时代日本对爵士乐的高水准诠释。专辑融合了AOR、放克与爵士融合元素，由顶级日本乐手共同呈现，原版在二手市场已炒至三位数价格。此次Wewantsounds厂牌的首个官方再版经过Colorsound Studio重新母带处理，保留原始封面设计，并附带了Paul Bowler撰写的新序言八页小册子。整体内容偏向商业化的高端流行爵士制作，虽然制作精良、阵容豪华，但在风格上属于主流范畴，与实验、前卫或地下音乐口味的关联有限。乐评本身更接近新闻稿性质的发行介绍，缺乏深度分析。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — After Roger Waters released "The dark side of the moon redux" in 2023, I couldn't help but noticehow one of the spoken word sections, specifically the one on the track "Speak to me (redux)",consists of the lyrics of. "Free four", but narrated inna grim, almost deathly way...this pinpointsto me how brilliant "Free four" actually is, the 1972 track released as a single tricks our minds inhow despite having upbeat, catchy, fun and relatively simple and silly instrumentation, that justacts as a veil to distract from the anxious, nihilistic and somber lyrics of the track.There really is no need to analyze the musicianship, the production (specially in remasteredversions, James Guthrie captures the Floyd essence with a flick of the wrist) or any of that, it'sPink Floyd, we cannot expect any less than high quality from them...so what I'll say is that thissingle shines just by how absurd the contrast is, it's brilliant, you can sing or hum the melodieswith ease and find yourself enjoying a nice pop song, and then at night find yourself questioningwhat you are even doing in life with it's lyrics, trying to fathom just how futile this all is...atfirst I didn't understand the single, now I do, it's a clever twist on what upbeat music should belike.Then we have "The gold it's in the...", I can't say much about the track, it's fun and catchy,compared to anything else Floyd made it's a piece of cake and really doesn't shine all that much,yet it's still enjoyable!It's a fun single, does a good job and has a clever twist, it can be anyone's cup of tea, I'll rateit 3/5 stars, mainly because the songs are fun but not that special compared to other art rock fromthat era, it's really good! And when you put it in context (soundtrack for the film "La Vall�e") youcan understand why it is the way it is.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / space rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评围绕Pink Floyd 1972年单曲《Free Four》展开，作者指出这首作品的精妙之处在于其表面的轻快旋律与歌词中虚无、焦虑主题之间的强烈反差。通过对比2023年Roger Waters《The Dark Side of the Moon Redux》中对这段念白的重新演绎，作者揭示了原曲在欢快编曲下隐藏的悲观内核。评论还顺带提及B面曲目，认为其相对平庸但仍具可听性。作者给予3/5星的评分，认为单曲在艺术摇滚范畴内有趣但并非特别突出。作为电影《La Vallée》的原声，整体风格服务于影片氛围。评论角度具有一定洞察力，但作品本身属于主流摇滚范畴，与实验、前卫、电子等偏好领域距离较远。

items.body: German synthrock act Antiage released the single “Leaving Babylon” on August 7, 2026. The song follows the band’s previous single “Zenith of Decay” and marks a shift in tone, from decay toward a fresh start. Leaving Babylon by Antiage “Leaving Babylon” is about the conscious decision to turn away from overwhelming noise. The single follows “Zenith of Decay”, released May 15, 2026, which Antiage described as a song about knowing when something tips over and choosing to stay in that state rather than looking for a way out or back. About Antiage Antiage is a synthpop and synthrock project from Friedrichroda, Thuringia, in Germany, formed around keyboardist and producer Veto Lestard (Sebastian Schulz). Schulz was previously a co-founder and long-time member of the EBM and IDM formation Mnemonic, which released albums on labels including Alfa Matrix, M-Tronic, Halbsicht and AntZen. Antiage released its debut single, “Lone”, in 2021 ahead of its debut album, combining electronica, melodic pop and rock. The band went on to release the album “Aphrodisiac Odyssey” on May 26, 2023, followed by “Pianistic Odyssey”, a piano-version companion release, on December 15, 2023. Antiage released the single “Zenith of Decay” on May 15, 2026, and followed it with “Leaving Babylon” on August 7, 2026.
items._cn_summary: 德国弗里德里希罗达的合成器流行/合成器摇滚项目Antiage由键盘手兼制作人Veto Lestard（Sebastian Schulz）主导，他此前是EBM与IDM团体Mnemonic的联合创始人和核心成员。乐队于2021年以单曲"Lone"出道，融合电子音乐、旋律流行与摇滚元素，先后发行专辑《Aphrodisiac Odyssey》（2023年5月）及钢琴版本《Pianistic Odyssey》（2023年12月）。新单曲"Leaving Babylon"于2026年8月7日发行，紧随同年5月的"Zenith of Decay"，主题聚焦于有意识地远离喧嚣、寻求新开始的转变，从颓败转向重启。本文为Side-Line刊载的新闻发布稿，侧重单曲发行信息与乐队背景介绍，缺乏对音乐本体（音色设计、编曲结构、制作水准等）的实质性评述。作为暗潮/EBM背景音乐人主导的合成器摇滚项目，虽与用户暗潮与电子口味有部分交集，但总体偏向旋律化流行路线，实验性与先锋性有限。

items.body: Project Silence, the industrial death metal band from Kuopio, Finland, released “Final Report (Purge)”, the second single from their upcoming fourth album. The track blends melodic death metal with retro-inspired synths and industrial metal, mixing blackened death vocals with melodic electronic elements. The band’s current lineup features vocalist, keyboardist and programmer D, guitarists S and A, drummer Silve_R and bassist H. Artwork for the single comes from Darkbringer Art. Second single since ‘Rotten’ “Final Report (Purge)” follows “Rotten“, the first single from the same forthcoming album, released in November 2025. The new album will be Project Silence’s fourth, following “The Void”, which combined industrial and synthwave melodies with groovy riffs. About Project Silence Project Silence was formed in Kuopio, Finland, in 2008 by vocalist Delacroix, later joined by Silve_R (Rieti Jauhiainen) on drums, S (Simo Ruotsalainen) and A (Aksu Mussalo) on guitars, and H (Henri Hakkarainen) on bass. The band mixes melodic death metal with the rhythmic, melancholic beats of synthwave and industrial music, a sound it developed across three albums, with combined streams passing two million on Spotify. Project Silence has played clubs and festivals including Kuopiorock and Mammothfest, and toured the UK, Russia and Latvia, opening for Aborted, Soilwork and Decapitated. Side-Line has followed the band’s singles cycle since “Disease” in 2022 and “Cult” in 2023, both ahead of “The Void”, and the lyric video for “Rip The Flesh” in 2024. “Final Report (Purge)”, released in August 2026, is the second single from the band’s fourth album, following “Rotten” in November 2025.

items.body:
SYEYL Introduces New Fuzzy Euphoric Electronica EP With 'limer' Via EELF Records

11 August 2026

Hrithik Arora aka SYEYL claims to have been "losing touch with his own artistic voice" before he found his way back with the upcoming EP 'Music Is The Answer', moving away from composing for function and bookings to reconnect with an emotive instinct. The choice pays off as the New Delhi-based artist manages to create focused and cohesive emotional worlds on the 5-track EP, especially unburdened by the need to include an excess of ideas in order to impress on the lead single 'limer'.

Shortened from the word "limerence", the track accordingly packs that sentimental dancefloor moment euphoria seen in the works of the likes of Bicep, Tom VR and some Four Tet. Simple rhythms of pristine digital textures syncopate against each other to create a sense of movement and rhythmic and harmonic ambience atop the four-to-the-floor groove, while the music video's early digital-camera aesthetic rounds out the nostalgic undercurrent in the music.

Watch the music video below and head to SYEYL's artist profile for more.

items._cn_summary: 这篇短文介绍了新德里艺术家SYEYL通过EELF Records厂牌发行的新EP《limerence》中的主打单曲《limer》。文章指出这位艺术家此前因忙于功能性作曲和商业演出而逐渐脱离了个人艺术表达，遂转向回归情感本真进行创作。这首标题取自"limerence"（恋爱般心醉状态）一词的曲目，试图营造类似Bicep、Tom VR和Four Tet作品中常见的感性舞池氛围。作品采用简洁的数字音色节奏相互切分，在四四拍律动之上构建出层次分明的节奏与和声空间，配合MV的早期数码相机美学，强化了音乐中的怀旧情绪。文章实质为新闻发布式的简短介绍，缺乏深入的音乐分析和评论。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur录制，是其第五张作品，以bal-musette风格为核心，广泛融合法国香颂、拉格泰姆、 jug band、 skiffle等多种早期二十世纪音乐语汇。乐队编制异常丰富，包括手风琴、萨克斯、班卓琴、尤克里里、锯琴、风笛等来自不同时代与地域的乐器，形成一种类似翻找老唱片重新编排的质感。27首短曲由Cravic以近似法国香颂传统的说唱方式演绎，其中既有1925年经典曲目，也有向法国抵抗运动女歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的原创作品，歌词内涵兼具幽默与庄重。评论指出，演奏者虽多为七旬老人，但以严肃的态度和热情复兴了这些被遗忘的风格，与Dan Hicks & His Hot Licks在精神上有相通之处。该专辑更接近复古拼贴与文化考古，与用户偏好的实验前卫路线交集有限，但其在乐器配置与跨时代风格混搭上展现出一定趣味性。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年曼彻斯特圣彼得广场大屠杀（彼得罗惨案）为题材，由Young 'Uns成员Sean Cooney创作原创歌曲，邀请Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter等音乐人合作。专辑以书籍形式呈现，包含历史信件、政治漫画和插图，构成多媒体事件。音乐方面，小型编制营造出强大声响，歌曲捕捉了集会当日的期待、兴奋以及骑兵冲入后转向恐惧与逃亡的转变，尾声充满悲怆与哀悼。歌词聚焦于Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等个人故事，三段短曲《The Monkey Rides The Mare》刻画士兵的傲慢与虚张声势。专辑在抗议活动受到压制的当下具有现实警示意义，历史细节留在书中，而音乐本身能够长久留存。整体属于英国工业民谣与历史叙事歌曲范畴。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: British electronic musician and producer William Orbit has died at the age of 69. His family confirmed he died at home on July 23, 2026. Orbit, born William Mark Wainwright on December 15, 1956, in Enfield, north London, is best known for producing Madonna’s 1998 album “Ray of Light” and for a series of remixes for artists across pop, rock and electronic music during the 1990s. Orbit’s family announced his death in a statement posted on social media: “William passed away at home on 23rd July, 2026. We are deeply saddened by his passing. He will be greatly missed by us and by so many whose lives he touched through his music, friendship, and kindness.” A cause of death has not been made public. Madonna paid tribute to Orbit on Instagram, writing: “He pressed a magic button inside of me and I fell into a galaxy of unrealized dreams. Your music gave me a magic carpet to fly on. You were my Ray of Light – as was my daughter Lola who was born around this time.” Among William Orbit’s many remix credits is his 1993 rework of Depeche Mode‘s “Walking in My Shoes”, released as the “Random Carpet Mix” and issued as part of the single’s release campaign for “Songs of Faith and Devotion”. About William Orbit William Orbit began his career in 1980 as a founding member of the ambient trio Torch Song, alongside Laurie Mayer and Grant Gilbert. He went on to score the 1986 film “Youngblood” and recorded as part of the dance act Bassomatic before establishing himself as a solo artist and in-demand remixer through the 1990s, working with artists including Madonna, U2, Kraftwerk, Nitzer Ebb and Blur. Orbit produced Madonna’s “Ray of Light” (1998), which won three Grammy Awards, and went on to work with her again on “Music” (2000) and “MDNA” (2012). He also produced Blur’s 1999 album “13” and delivered two UK number-one singles for All Saints, “Pure Shores” and “Black Coffee”. His solo output includes the long-running “Strange Cargo” series and the classical-crossover project “Pieces in a Modern Style”. His most recent solo album, “The Painter”, was released in 2022.
items._cn_summary: 本文为英国电子音乐制作人William Orbit的讣告新闻稿，而非乐评。文章回顾了其生平与职业生涯：他于1980年创立ambient三人组Torch Song，后涉足电影配乐与舞曲项目Bassomatic，九十年代成为炙手可热的混音师与制作人。他曾为Madonna制作1998年专辑《Ray of Light》（获三座格莱美）、Blur的《13》以及All Saints的两首英国冠军单曲，个人作品涵盖《Strange Cargo》系列与《Pieces in a Modern Style》等古典跨界项目。其混音作品如Depeche Mode《Walking in My Shoes》的Random Carpet Mix体现了九十年代电子改编的典型手法。Madonna在悼念中形容他按下了一个魔法按钮。文章侧重人物生平与商业成就介绍，缺乏对其音乐技法、声音设计或艺术理念的深入分析，对实验电子听众参考价值有限。

items.body: German synth-pop duo Purwien & Kowa release the single “Hinter Glas” on August 14, 2026 via Town And Towers Records. The track is a new version of “Hinter Glas,” a song originally released by Christian Purwien’s earlier band Second Decay, and arrives ahead of the duo’s sixth studio album, “Sechs,” due October 9, 2026 on the same label. The digital single carries three tracks: “Hinter Glas,” a remix of “Eyes Of Aragon” by Swedish electronic duo CRED, and a 12″ mix of “Hinter Glas.” “Eyes Of Aragon” was originally recorded by No Comment, the German synth-pop band Thomas Kowa played in from 1989. The single is available on major streaming services through this link. Purwien & Kowa reunite Second Decay and No Comment on ‘Hinter Glas’ “Hinter Glas” first appeared on Second Decay‘s 1993 maxi-CD of the same name and again a year later on the album “Taste,” the German wave/electronic act Christian Purwien co-founded with Andreas Michael Sippel in 1987. With Purwien & Kowa, Purwien re-recorded his own song while Thomas Kowa brought in a remix of “Eyes Of Aragon” from his former band No Comment, handled by CRED. The pairing puts a track from each half of the duo’s back catalogue on a single release. Purwien & Kowa describe their own sound as “retro analogue synth pop without hair.” “Hinter Glas” follows the single “Concorde” as the second preview of “Sechs,” the duo’s sixth studio album, due October 9, 2026 via Town And Towers Records. The band also runs the Disko 80 podcast with Purwien and Kowa as hosts, and records as Heldautomat as a side project. About Purwien & Kowa Purwien & Kowa is a German synth-pop duo based in Dortmund formed by Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa. Purwien co-founded the electronic/darkwave act Second Decay in 1987, initially under the name Blue Velvet, together with Andreas Michael Sippel. Second Decay released the tape “Monochromes” in 1988 and the 12-inch “Killing Desire” in 1989, followed by “La Décadence Électronique” on CD in 1992, the “Hinter Glas” maxi-CD in 1993 and the album “Taste” in 1994. The band continued with “Der Nerv” in 1995, “Familiar” in 1997, “The Hunt” and “De Luxe” in 1998, “Hotels” in 1999 and “Kaltes, weißes Licht” in 2001, before pausing new material after the 2002 live release “Zwischenfall 1999.” Thomas Kowa, born Thomas Kowalzik in 1969 in Ludwigshafen am Rhein, joined the German synth-pop band No Comment in 1989 and has lived in Switzerland since 2007. He founded the label Nanopop in 2001, closing it in 2007 to focus on writing; since 2012 he has published a series of crime novels and thrillers. His other current music projects include Nine Seconds and Emily Kinski’s dead. Purwien and Kowa began recording together as Purwien & Kowa, releasing the three-EP digital set “Drei” via Zwei Records in October 2018. The duo also co-hosts the Disko 80 podcast, which covers 1980s music and has featured more than 100 episodes with guests including Joachim Witt, Bernhard Lloyd of Alphaville and Marcus Meyn of Camouflage. Kowa separately co-hosts the “Krimi Schweiz” podcast on Swiss crime fiction. Purwien & Kowa returned in 2026 with the single “Concorde,” followed by “Hinter Glas,” ahead of their sixth studio album “Sechs,” due October 9, 2026 via Town And Towers Records.

items.body: German electronic duo Heldautomat released the single “Anders Sein” on August 14, 2026 via Town & Towers Records. The track is a new interpretation of “Anders Sein,” originally released by Second Decay in 1994 on the album “Taste.” The release includes a classic 12-inch mix as a digital B-side. Heldautomat is Christian Purwien (vocals and lyrics) and Thomas Kowa (synthesizers and songs). Purwien co-founded Second Decay with Andreas Sippel in 1987, and “Anders Sein” appeared on Second Decay’s 1994 album “Taste” alongside “I Hate Berlin” and “Hinter Glas.” The new Heldautomat version is built around analogue synthesizers, piano and minimalist drum-machine rhythms, keeping the melody of the original while giving the arrangement more space. “Anders Sein” follows Heldautomat’s debut single, “Am ersten Tag,” released in May 2026. The duo’s debut album, “Zwischen den Lichtern,” is scheduled for autumn 2026 and will include eleven tracks sung in German and English. “Anders Sein” is available to stream and purchase via all platforms and on Bandcamp. About Heldautomat Heldautomat is a German electronic duo formed by Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa. Purwien began his recording career in 1987 as co-founder and vocalist of Second Decay, a project originally named Blue Velvet, alongside Andreas Sippel. Working exclusively with analogue synthesizers, Second Decay released the tape “Monochromes” in 1988, the 12-inch “Killing Desire” in 1989, the CD “La Décadence Électronique” in 1992, the maxi-CD “Hinter Glas” in 1993 and the album “Taste” in 1994, the release that introduced “Anders Sein.” Second Decay’s second album, “The Hunt,” originally released in 1996, was reissued by Emmobiz Records as a green double LP with bonus tracks in November 2025, and a second vinyl edition of “Taste” followed via Emmo.Biz Records in 2026. Thomas Kowa is a music producer, synthesizer player and thriller author whose Erik Lindberg crime series is available in audiobook form; he has previously worked with No Comment and Nine Seconds. Purwien and Kowa first collaborated as Purwien & Kowa, releasing five albums together, including “Zwei,” the three-part “Drei” series and “Vier.” In February 2026, Purwien & Kowa performed at the 18th Elektrisch Festival in Zwickau. Heldautomat, launched in 2026 with the single “Am ersten Tag,” is described by the duo as a darker and more uncompromising direction than their earlier collaborative work, built around analogue synthesizers, piano and minimalist drum-machine rhythms. “Anders Sein” is the project’s second single, revisiting a track from Purwien’s own back catalogue ahead of the debut Heldautomat album “Zwischen den Lichtern,” due in autumn 2026.

items.body: Rome released its tenth studio album, “The Hyperion Machine,” on 12 August 2016 through Trisol Music Group. The neofolk album turns 10 this year. It followed the mini-album “Coriolan,” released on 1 April 2016, and arrived as the tenth studio album in a decade of releases that began with 2006’s “Nera.” Rome recorded “The Hyperion Machine” at Ear We Go Studio in Belgium. The 11-track album runs 47 minutes and includes “The Hyperion Machine,” “Celine in Jerusalem,” “Transference,” “The Alabanda Breviary,” “Stillwell” featuring Swedish vocalist Thåström, “Cities of Asylum,” “Skirmishes for Diotima,” “Adamas,” “The Secret Germany (For Paul Celan),” “Die Mörder Mühsams” and the bonus track “FanFanFan,” a cover of a Thåström song. Jérôme Reuter wrote all the other tracks. Trisol issued the album on CD and vinyl LP, including an orange vinyl edition and a later white vinyl pressing, and it streams on Spotify. Side-Line’s 2016 review of the album rated it 8½ out of 10. About Rome Jérôme Reuter, born 2 August 1981 in Luxembourg, founded Rome in November 2005 as an outlet for his own songs, taking the project’s name from an abridged version of his first name. He had previously recorded as Reggie Fain, played in the Oi! band the Skinflicks and fronted the post-punk act Mack Murphy and the Inmates. Rome signed to the Swedish label Cold Meat Industry in 2006 and released the EP “Berlin” and the debut album “Nera” that year, followed by “Confessions d’un Voleur d’Ames” in 2007, co-produced with Patrick Damiani. Nikos Mavridis joined Reuter and Damiani in 2009, the same year Rome signed to the German label Trisol and released the EP “To Die Among Strangers” and the acoustic-based album “Flowers from Exile.” Rome issued the EP “Hate Us and See If We Mind” in 2013, followed in 2014 by “A Passage to Rhodesia,” released as a box set of two CDs, a 10-inch vinyl single and a DVD containing music videos and an interview with Reuter. The mini-album “Coriolan,” inspired by Shakespeare’s “Coriolanus,” followed on 1 April 2016, and “The Hyperion Machine” arrived that August as Rome’s tenth studio album. Rome went on to release “Hall of Thatch” in January 2018, “Parlez-Vous Hate?” in January 2021, “Gates of Europe” in August 2023 and the mini-album “World in Flames” in July 2024, and issued three further albums – “Civitas Solis,” “The Hierophant” and “The Tower” – in April 2025, extending a catalog that now runs to more than twenty studio releases as “The Hyperion Machine” marks its tenth year.
items._cn_summary: 本文是一篇纪念性质的文章，报道Rome乐队第十张录音室专辑《The Hyperion Machine》发行十周年。文章主要罗列了专辑的基本信息：2016年8月12日通过Trisol厂牌发行，11首曲目共47分钟，在比利时Ear We Go Studio录制，词曲由主创Jérôme Reuter创作，并提及与瑞典歌手Thåström的合作。内容以发行信息和乐队发展史为主，缺乏对音乐本身的深入分析、未探讨专辑的创作理念或声响特色，也未评论其艺术价值。文章还简要回顾了Rome自2005年成立以来的唱片目录及成员变动，更接近一份乐队百科式的事实陈述，而非具有深度洞察力的乐评。

items.body: New Jersey band Deardarkhead unveiled a video for “In Another Life”, a track from their album “The Pendulum Swings”, out now on their own imprint Fertile Crescent Records. The video was directed by Italian video artist Francesca Bonci, known for work with Federale, The Dandy Warhols and Slowdive’s Rachel Goswell. “The Pendulum Swings” is Deardarkhead’s second full-length album, arriving almost three decades after their 1998 debut, “Unlock the Valves of Feeling”, also issued on Fertile Crescent Records. It was recorded at Miner Street Recordings in Philadelphia and produced, engineered and mixed by Brian McTear and Amy Morrissey, known for their work with The War on Drugs, Kurt Vile and Sharon Van Etten, and mastered by Joe Lambert, whose credits include Animal Collective, Blonde Redhead, Beach House, M83 and Wild Nothing. The album is streaming on Spotify, Apple Music and Bandcamp, with CD, digital and 180-gram vinyl editions available for pre-order. The Pendulum Swings by Deardarkhead Deardarkhead’s current lineup on ‘The Pendulum Swings’ Deardarkhead’s current lineup features guitarist Kevin Harrington and drummer Robert Weiss, joined by bassist James Malizia, who replaced Brandon Howard after the album was recorded. Drummer Robert Weiss described the record as a mix of older and newer material: “‘The Pendulum Swings’ is a collection of both older and newer material that we are very proud of. Each song has its own distinct vibe, but they collectively make up the DDH sound. This was the second time we recorded at Miner Street Recordings and we focused on trying new things with drum loops, different time signatures, backing keyboard tracks, using an ebow and bass VI, plus more guitar tracks than ever.” Deardarkhead had earlier shared the album’s lead track, “Letting Go”, featuring keyboardist Joe McGinty of The Psychedelic Furs and Nada Surf on additional layers. About Deardarkhead Deardarkhead formed in 1988 in Atlantic City, New Jersey. The band takes its name from “Cean Dubh Dilis”, an 1867 Irish poem by Samuel Ferguson. After early cassette releases, Deardarkhead debuted with the full-length “Unlock the Valves of Feeling” in 1998 through their own imprint, Fertile Crescent Records, the first of five recordings the band issued on that label. Vocalist Michael Amper left the band in 2009, after which Deardarkhead shifted to a fully instrumental, texture-driven approach centered on guitar and atmosphere. Captured Tracks released a retrospective of the band’s early material, “Oceanside: 1991-1993”, in 2011 as part of its Shoegaze Archives series. Deardarkhead joined Saint Marie Records for the “Strange Weather” EP in 2016. Over the years the band has played shows alongside Supergrass, The Psychedelic Furs, Everclear, Nothing and The Lilys. “The Pendulum Swings”, released through Fertile Crescent Records, is Deardarkhead’s first full-length album since “Unlock the Valves of Feeling”, and the video for “In Another Life” is the latest piece of material the band has shared from it.

items.body: Welp. Better late than never. It's Kvlt Kolvmn's a-bit-more-than-halfway through 2026 best of list! Strap into your frostiest pair of dungaroos. It's gonna get wild.Black metal has had a very curious year for me. While I would say about half of the records I've listened to in the genre have felt like all-time bangers, the other half have put me to sleep. So in honor of that, I'll be presenting half a top 10 list. You're welcome. More awesome, however, is Boeli's incredible top 10, which features a handful of records I had yet to hear prior to reading his selections. Let's just say that good taste abounds as his list unfolds.But no more delay. Here are our iciest picks of 2026 so far.Stay frosty.-Jonathan AdamsTop Albums of 2026 So FarJonathan’s ListSaidan - Fangdriller: Scars Beneath Memory’s WristAs made plain when I waxed ineloquent a few weeks ago regarding the benefits of embracing the cringe in your life, I’m a BIG fan of Saidan. I would contend that their four album run thus far is one of the most consistently impressive in recent black metal, with each record refining and tactfully building upon what came before. Given this dynamic, it should come as no surprise that Fangdriller: Scars Beneath Memory’s Wrist is not only the band’s most complete and fantastic album thus far, but also the best extreme music record of the year so far. For me, it’s not close. What Saidan manages to channel here is a superb blend of melodic black metal, punk aesthetics, and power metal speed (replete with memorable hooks, punchy breakdowns, and manically aggressive tremolo shred sessions). It’s a relatively unique mixture that works due to genuinely gorgeous songwriting, which allows each sound to coexist seamlessly and interdependently without giving the listener genre-bending whiplash. The base is always black metal, and Saidan writes like a black metal band expanding the margins of the genre’s template with tasteful aggression. But their inclusion of other styles only works to sharpen and deepen listeners’ immersion in the world they’re creating. There isn’t a dull moment on this thing, and I frequently find myself hitting play again immediately after “Memory” fades into static. It’s addictive as hell. And, ultimately, that’s what I want from a record. I want to be transported, invited into a sonic world that’s cohesive enough to keep my undivided attention, and varied enough to never feel stale. And that’s exactly what Saidan provide with this absolute gem of a record. It’s my favorite thing I’ve heard so far this year, and I have a hard time imagining it being supplanted. Melodic black metal perfection.  FANGDRILLER: Scars Beneath Memory's Wrist by Saidan Miserere Luminis - SideraSpeaking of immersion, few albums so far this year have gripped me to the degree that Sidera, the third full-length from Montreal-based Miserere Luminis, has. Man oh man is this an exquisite slab of melody-heavy and deeply atmospheric black metal. The compositions are simply fantastic, winding and building into a delicious labyrinth of emotionally devastating delight. The musicianship on display here is also superb, allowing these tracks to breathe in the appropriate places before laying the black metal hammer down to glorious effect. It’s a fantastic showing from a band that has yet to release a dud, and I cannot wait to see where they transport us next.  Sidera by Miserere Luminis Worm - NecropalaceOne of the most hyped and ballyhooed records of the first half of 2026, I was honestly ready to judge this thing pretty harshly given initial impressions I’d heard from friends around the band's shift in tone. Happy to say I was dead wrong, as Necropalace feels like the most natural direction in the world for Worm to go after spending significant time with it. In a similar vein to Fangdriller, this record is just FUN. The songwriting is gothic and propulsive, creating an almost theatrical atmosphere that’s deeply enjoyable to sit in. One would never have guessed at Worm’s doomy roots by hearing Necropalace, thus is its genuine quality as a black metal album. Can’t recommend it highly enough, and plan on giving this thing many more spins throughout the year.  Necropalace (24-bit HD audio) by Worm Ultha - A Light So DimUltha is one of the most unpredictable and strangely amazing collectives working in the black metal sphere today, and A Light So Dim is unequivocally their boldest experiment to date. Thankfully, it works on almost every level. While the tonal shifts may look jarring on paper, Ultha’s unique skill of pulling various sound tapestries and weaving them into a robust whole is on full display here, and there isn’t a thing I’d change about this record. It is a long journey, which may be off-putting to some. But rest assured the time will be well spent. This is my favorite of the group’s records so far and a musical odyssey well worth taking. Genuinely brilliant stuff from these German geniuses.  A Light So Dim by ULTHA Misotheist - De PinteWell, enough pansy ass beautiful/experimental poser black metal, amirite?? JK naturally. While I’m a huge fan of bands that push the black metal formula to the fringes of trve, I’m still a devotee of the core sonic nastiness that made this genre the pariah it is in the music world. Enter Misotheist and their brilliant fourth full-length outing De Pinte. Like your black metal with a hefty dose of buzzsaw dissonance and tremolo violence? You’re in luck! This record absolutely slays. The first three tracks in particular are nothing short of a masterclass in black metal done right, with enough audio violence to sate even the thirstiest fan. But it’s the records fourth cut that shows the band’s capabilities most notably, presenting a doomier side that slows down the tempo but never once minimizes the menace or aggression these enigmatic Norwegians are known for. It’s a brilliant album that has received many a spin from yours truly and a true highlight of 2026.  De Pinte by Misotheist Boeli’s Kvlt kolvmn Top 10: Where Kvltvre Goes to Feed the Vvltvres10. Einherjer - LifebloodBy virtue of another folk-tinged black metal indebted band not making the cut for reasons of probable sketch, Einherjer just made my top 10 spot even though it’s hardly been out long enough to form a proper opinion.One thing I can say without hesitation, is that I quite enjoy the Norwegian Viking metallers trajectory since I last actively listened to them about a decade ago. While Av Oss, For Oss was an occasionally engaging if fairly monotone exercise in mid-paced black metal, Lifeblood is a much more colorful and generally more dynamic and melodic affair, and while still rooted in black metal, the branches of its world tree sapling have grown to embrace heavy metal and folk metal more and more. I appreciate their more melodic and varied approach, and would appreciate it even more with some more tempo variation and a bit of judicious editing. That being said, there are times I long for this subgenre like no other, and this year Einherjer have been its prime deliverer so far.  Lifeblood by Einherjer 9. Burnt Lodge / Veytik - Anchors Plunged Off Helluland (Split)Another somewhat late entry, I had almost completely missed this release, and was well and truly excited when I saw Burnt Lodge had new stuff out. Their 2024 release Intergenerational Anamnesis is one of my favourite iterations of Native American Black Metal. This particular micro-genre is a particular favorite of mine, and alongside Blackbraid and Nechochwen, Burnt Lodge sits among its top practitioners. Had this been a full album,. And had I discovered it earlier, this one might have sat quite a bit higher.While I also quite enjoy Veytik’s thrasher, Hellenic and Obsequiaesque escapades, they have not yet managed to grab me like Burnt Lodge does.  Anchors Plunged Off Helluland (Split) by Burnt Lodge 8. Pure Wrath - Bleak Days AheadI shall lazily refer you to my previous musings on Pure Wrath’s latest in Mays Kvlt Kolvmn.  Bleak Days Ahead by Pure Wrath 7. Stormkeep - The Nocturnes of IswylmOn their latest, bombasically titled album, Stormkeep took me by storm out of the gate, although I’m not yet wholly sure they’ll remain in my top 10 for the year entire. I generally like my black metal adorned with a serious amount of low-end, contrary to its traditional sound. While Stormkeep toe the line of what I enjoy production wise, the mix of spooky whimsy, expansive songwriting and exhilarating choruses managed to perk my ears up considerably. The gruff, charming and incredibly catchy gang shouts of opener “The Taste of Immortal Blood” are choice as hell, and while I could do with some more hooks like those to get my very mortal blood a-pumping in the mid section before the last two tracks offer a convincing coda, I suspect the album may need some more time to gestate before it truly settles in. The Nocturnes Of Iswylm by Stormkeep 6. Antrisch - Expedition III: RenitenzpfadAtmospheric black metal might be one of the most oversaturated and justly maligned sub-genres, but when done right, it can also be one of it’s most powerful. Of course your definition of “right” will vary, and there are many roads to Rome. Enter Antrisch, whose take on the sub-genre is one I would use as a prime example of doing atmoblack well. Antrisch unleash a vicious, razor-sharp blackened assault, while adorning their music with a powerful, iterative concept of (historical) exploration of some very inhospitable environments.While previous album Die Passage’s arctic voyage was an obvious fit for Antrisch’s icy timbre, Renitenzpfad might be equally if not more exciting for its less obvious theme of the hardships endured and horrors dished out by Spanish colonisers in the Americas. With all of Antrisch’s biting venom, this time empowered by topical and tasteful atmospheric interludes, sampling and thematic instrumentation, they once again succeed in telling a story and immersing their audience in it, without ever diluting their vicious, energetic core sound. Smart, urgent, dynamic and varied, while remaining remarkably cohesive;  Expedition III is another successful iteration in these Germans’ discography. EXPEDITION III : Renitenzpfad by Antrisch 5. Ashbringer - SubglacialI stand by my original review; anything close to 2019s Absolution would have topped any list, whether Black Metal specific or not. Time has both made me lost sight of Subglacial (who releases an album in January, I ask you!?), while also softening my initial dashed expectations for another long-form atmoblack magnum opus. My expectations should not make for a good or bad album in the end, and Ashbringer’s wintry yet somehow warm and nostalgic 2026 release is absolutely a good album. Go listen to it if you haven’t yet, and then go listen to Absolution.  Subglacial by Ashbringer 4. Apolaustic - No Plenitude Without SufferingWere it not for a scheduling snafu on my end, I would have reviewed this melodic black metal gem in April, and could now get away with another short referral to something I wrote before. Alas, no luck. I did not, and you shall now suffer my relative plenitude. I picked up the promo for this album based on a promising single at the time, and was further pleasantly surprised by an album that proved deep and expansive enough that I was still forming a full opinion by teh time the review deadline slipped through my powerless fingers. A couple months later, I can tell you with full confidence that this is my favourite “pure” melodic black metal album of the year so far, defining meloblack in the vein of something like Mare Cognitum or Houle. Decidedly less maritime (in title or sound) and with a much more space-faring vibe going on, Apolaustic’s ability to write dynamic songs with an undeniably kinetic mix of melody, technicality and songwriting chops should be no surprise to anyone who is familiar with project mastermind Romain Negro’s previous membership of excellent progressive/medloic/technical death metal band Stortregn.Indeed, comparing No Plenitude Without Suffering to Stortregn’s younger black metal sibling would not be entirely inappropriate, as it exhibits the same mix of soul, shred and sheer scope, if so far lacking absolute supernova’s like "Grand Nexion Abyss” or “Xeno Chaos”.For any enjoyers of melodic black metal of quality and pedigree unfuckwithable, look no further. But please do actually, there’s three more entries. No Plenitude Without Suffering by APOLAUSTIC 3. Hellripper - CoronachAs it stomps, gallops and jigs between fun, fury and a finisher of true grandeur, since I last covered it in April’s KK Helripper’s Coronach has proven both it’s endlessly engaging vibrancy, and its ability to engage so many of the things that can make a metal album great, but rarely show up on the same album. It’s fun, it’s solemn and majestic, it's catchy, it’s angry, it brims with energy and sounds like it’s about to rip out of its restraints, but never gets speed metal sloppy. Incredibly varied yet uniformly great, Coronach should show up in quite a few lists come year’s end, and not just the blackened ones.  Coronach (24-bit HD audio) by Hellripper 2. The Silver - Looking Glass Hymnal BlueI honestly have no idea if this is even black metal, which is also the only reason it’s not on number one. The Silver’s sophomore amalgamation of metal styles is the kind of breath-taking bricolage that makes me want to rip up my clothes and howl at the moon. Rooted in a deep romanticism, indulgent, baroque, gothic and maximalist yet never tasteless, this album embodies what I love in my heavy music while eschewing everything I don’t.Considering its members comprise veterans of Horrendous (recognize those eardrum-flayingly awesome shrieks yet?) and Crypt Sermon, the quality is perhaps not as surprising, but while neither of those other projects fully mesh with my preferences, this one really, really does.The only criticism I would level at it is that “Tow Candles” and “My Lone Dark Lantern” are simply so good that they threaten to cast shadows as dark as their lights are bright, and thus obscure their surrounding companions.  Looking Glass Hymnal Blue by The Silver 1. Miserere Luminis - SideraBut of course, my pride as a genre stickler could not survive placing anything at number oen that is not unequivocally BLACK METAL.Luckily, there is nothing disingenuous about this placement. Miserere Luminis, another stellar band out of Quebec (seriously, what’s the secret??) gracefully take the year’s twisted yet mesmerisingly beautiful throne. With an ear for blackened melodic rapture akin to Houle, riffs as snaky and entrancing as late-stage Ulcerate and the soul-rending cathartic qualities of Selbst,Sidera goes above and beyond its influences, featuring truly engrossing compositions replete with strings and probably my favorite drumming of the year so far. Gorgeous, sad and fragile without losing the razor-sharp bite that atmospheric black metal so often lacks, I have no doubt this tour-de-force will remain at or near the top come final list season, and stay in rotation far beyond the year’s end. Sidera by Miserere Luminis

items.body: Review by SilverLight59 — Some albums are designed to keep the evening rolling, and others to gently wind the evening down. This one falls squarely in this latter category and does so with style and grace. Bruce Soord requires little introduction. As the anchor behind The Pineapple Thief, he has spent over two decades immersed in the modern Crossover Prog subgenre. His solo work, however, represents a deliberate departure from the intricate full-band dynamics of his main project. This, his third solo release, Luminescence, strips away the technical, rhythmically complex frameworks, propelling percussion and drumming, often associated with the Pineapple Thief to explore a quieter, deeply introspective sonic landscape. While it leans heavily into acoustic textures, incorporates lush string arrangements, and at times runs somewhat in parallel with accessible mainstream structures, the album still maintains a sophisticated harmonic depth that will resonate with fans of atmospheric art rock.If you pay attention to the lyrics, you will find that the album outlines a clear narrative arc, guiding the listener through a journey that begins with the anxious realization of fleeting time on "Dear Life," descends into urban isolation and grief, and ultimately resolves in a peaceful state of closure on "Find Peace". This emotional trajectory is held together by Soord's intimate vocal delivery; his singing style acts as the perfect vessel for his lyrics, conveying an authentic vulnerability that makes the heavy themes feel profoundly personal, and yet he is letting us in. Ultimately, by trading complex rock structures for softer more acoustic arrangements, he has crafted an album defined by its smooth edges and mellow accessibility.So, lets take a brief look at the tracks.Dear Life: The opener here begins with a gentle acoustic strumming pattern, builds a bit to a modest pace, mellow and accessible, and falls directly in crossover territory. Soord's vocals are inviting and emotive. Lyrically, it begins the album's thematic arc of the complexities of life, aging, and the fragile value of one's existence. As a comparison, it might be compared with the melodic sensibilities of Porcupine Tree tracks like "Lazarus." A pretty start. (9/10)Lie Flat: This piece layers atmospheric synth sound beat around Soord's reverbed vocals. It balances a linear vocal melody with unpredictable instrumental textures, isolated guitar work, and periodic forward keyboard sequences. While a restrained work, it will prove to be one of the more dynamic tracks. Again, there is a certain Porcupine Tree & Steven Wilson vocal quality, while the musical structure is bit more in the field of late-era Anathema. Lyrically, it reflects personal clarity and finding unspoken truths later in life. Another very nice track. (9.5/10)Olomouc: Another standout track that begins with sparse acoustic guitar before an expansive, breathtaking chorus section swells into view. The sophisticated orchestration provides the harmonic complexity that provides an engaging depth to the track. The lyrics and chorus are outstanding and memorable. While highly accessible, there is a nice progressive edge delivering this nicely into the symphonic art rock flavor.Another winning track. (9.5/10)So Simple: A very short stripped down piece. Living up to its name, this song relies on a direct, infectious melody. It is arguably the most mainstream friendly track on the record, sacrificing progressive exercises for immediate, pure emotional connection. Compared to the three opening tracks, this seems to be a musical and emotional respite that allows the album twist to some different dynamics to follow. (8/10) Never Ending Light: This track shifts the dynamics with an eerie, slow-burning ambient groove. The keys here have a bit of a sinister edge, the guitars have a bit of discordance and individual tracking creating a fascinating listen. The vocal harmonies and minor-key shifts here evoke a strong Radiohead influence, making it structurally simple but texturally and productionally sophisticated. Another great track. (9/10)Day of all Days: An acoustic-heavy piece that feels like a classic, melancholic Pineapple Thief ballad. Once it build from the acoustic opening, it gains some musical fullness in sections, and then drops back to the acoustic side. This is again an accessible piece that relies on an emotional vocal hook rather than edgy time signature changes. In Addition to the Pineapple thief comparison, one might also see a bit of a parallel to Riverside's softer acoustic moments. (8.5/10)Nestle In: Flirting with a electronica type rhythm, this stands as the album's most upbeat track by a slight margin. The drumming is the most forward here than on any other track in this offering, giving this offering the most propulsion. Not wildly so, but noticeable. There is also a nice guitar amplification near the end, again the strongest of the album. Built on a minimalist, electronic pulse, it bridges the gap between accessible trip-hop rhythms and subtle avant garde art-rock elements. (8/10)Instant Flash of Light: A considerable contrast to the preceding track, this is a haunting sparse song featuring a delicate acoustic center layered with subtle, cinematic strings. It strips away prog pretense for accessible somewhat pastoral sounding singer-songwriter architecture. There is a gradual build in intensity that is refreshing and a highlight, but it still stays well within the boundaries of restraint. This is a nice ballad, but it seems a bit simple compared to the previous tracks. (7.75/10)Rushing: Another track where the acoustic guitar takes center stage, more upbeat this time. Some nice note picking over the top. This picks up the feeling of the song title as there is a push to the flow of the song. As an instrumental piece this seems to serve as a pleasant bridge leading into the concluding portion of the album. (7.5/10)Stranded Here: This Features a slow cinematic build that immediately conjures a kinship with the likes of Sigur Ros both musically and vocally. The slow motion atmospherics provide a satisfying nod to post-rock structures. The gentle acoustic guitar and underlying synth wash and strings are both lovely and immersive. This is easy to get lost in. Another understated highlight (9.25/10)Read to Me: This piece feels born out of the previous as they are similar in tone and tempo. A brief, atmospheric piece that leans heavily into ambient space and sound design. The vocals have an ethereal warmth that is quite alluring, and although very accessible, should appeal even to prog purists who appreciate thoughtful texturing and arrangements. (8.5/10)Find Peace: The closer that brings the record to a wonderful, cinematic conclusion. The slow, soaring strings bring a soft intensity that emphasize the central theme of the album arc, that of letting go and finding inner tranquility. The lyrics and vocals captivate these feelings and leave the listener enlightened and pondering the deeper things of life. The concluding minute winds down with discordant string notes, and the final 10 seconds ends with the opening notes of the first song to create a loop, and so life is, a loop it seems. (8.5/10)Well, what to say? This is a consistently beautiful album in a highly accessible prog and art rock type of way. It could be argued that it is more mainstream than not, but the depth and layering of the tracks suggest otherwise. It is interesting that Soord's solo material is a complete deviation from the bombast of The Pineapple Thief so don't be looking for that here. And there are no epics here. Everything clocks in at three to four minutes or even less. Even so, there is some surprising evolutions within the songs. From a strict progressive rock perspective, Luminescence may come across to some as too narrow in its pacing and overall dynamics. Listeners looking for technical virtuosity, jagged guitar solos, or the complex time signatures of traditional prog may find the record overly safe. The fairly consistent tempo and generally acoustic arrangements if not listened to purposefully may tend to blend together, creating beautiful sonic wallpaper. On the other hand, for those who like a milder form of prog, and are willing to deep dive into it, there is a tremendous lot to like here. One of the album's greatest strengths lies in its immaculate production, pristine sound and mixing, and its emotional honesty. Soord's vocal performance is exceptionally warm, and Andrew Skeet's orchestration elevates the material significantly. Luminescence is a gorgeous testament to Bruce Soord's maturity as a composer, offering a masterwork in atmospheric crossover prog. So, in conclusion, while this may lack the technical fireworks required to satisfy fans of avant-garde or symphonic prog, its pristine sound design, thematic cohesion, and rich textures offer a deeply rewarding listen for fans of modern, atmospheric art rock. In my opinion, highly recommended for those moments when you are looking for some prog serenity. Maybe just slightly under 4 stars, but we will round it up because 3 just simply won't do.

items.body: Irish synth-pop artist Paul Quin has signed to Town And Towers Records for his second album, “HIVEMIND”, set for release in December 2026 on digital, CD and vinyl. The Copenhagen label will issue a new single each month starting at the end of September, with the album following in December. The lead single, “Dancing With The Devil”, has been shared with press ahead of the release schedule. “HIVEMIND” arrives five years after Quin’s debut album “Life On Earth”, released in 2021 on the Russian electronica label ScentAir Records. According to the press release, the new album’s title refers to “groupthink” and “conformity of thinking” in internet culture, continuing as a theme across the record. UK producer and mixer Mark Saunders, credited on previous work with David Bowie, Erasure, Human League and Cyndi Lauper, came out of what the press release describes as semi-retirement to co-write and produce a series of tracks with Quin. DJ and former Royseven guitarist Eamonn “Jabbawookie” Barrett also co-wrote and produced tracks for the record. Additional credited collaborators include Dec Quinn of Republic of Loose, who co-wrote “Ordinary Love”; string arranger Gav Moran, who contributed to “1986”; punk musician Pete Holidai, who produced a cover of MGMT’s “Kids”; sound engineer Greg Malocca; and Aidan Casserly of Empire State Human and songwriter Colm Key, both previous collaborators of Quin’s. ‘HIVEMIND’ tracklist According to the press release, the twelve tracks run: “Half A Man”, “I Promise”, “People Look Better At Night”, “Dancing With The Devil”, “Blood Stained Dream”, “Gods”, “Little Brother”, “1986”, “Alex”, “Friday Night For Lovers”, “Ordinary Love” and “Bray (Candyfloss And Lucozade)”. About Paul Quin Paul Quin is an Irish singer, songwriter and producer who has released Irish electronic music since the late 1980s. He first performed as lead singer of the synth-pop duo BiaZarre with John Butler, whose double A-side single “A Better Place / The Colour of Rain” was released in 1989. Butler died in 1998 of an AIDS-related illness. After a decade away from music, Quin returned with his debut solo album “Life On Earth”, released in 2021 on ScentAir Records and co-written and co-produced with Aidan Casserly of Empire State Human. The album was preceded by a re-recorded version of “A Better Place” as its first single, and its songs drew on themes of loss, bereavement, addiction and homelessness, with lyrics informed by Quin’s experience as a gay man in Ireland. In an interview with GCN (Gay Community News), Quin described the album as “a kind of a personal renaissance.” Quin has now signed to Town And Towers Records, a Copenhagen-based label specialising in Nordic dark wave, synthpop, dark synth, italo disco, future pop and electro pop, for his second album “HIVEMIND”. The label plans to release a new single monthly from the end of September 2026, leading up to the album’s release in December 2026 on digital, CD and vinyl formats. The current single, “Dancing With The Devil”, was shared directly with Side-Line ahead of its release. More information is available on Quin’s official website.
items._cn_summary: 爱尔兰合成器流行艺人Paul Quin签约哥本哈根厂牌Town And Towers，宣布第二张专辑《HIVEMIND》将于2026年12月发行。专辑概念围绕网络文化中的群体思维与从众心理展开，十二首曲目涵盖从情感到社会议题的多元主题。制作阵容颇为引人注目：英国制作人Mark Saunders曾与David Bowie、Erasure、Human League合作，此次复出参与多首曲目的创作与制作；DJ兼前Royseven吉他手Eamonn Barrett也参与联合创作；此外还有Republic of Loose的Dec Quinn、弦乐编曲Gav Moran、朋克音乐人Pete Holidai等客座合作者。首支单曲《Dancing With The Devil》已在发行前提供给媒体。作为Quin继2021年首张专辑《Life On Earth》后的新作，该专辑延续了他对失落、悲伤、成瘾等主题的个人化书写。
